security_audit.summary: Twenty-nine static alerts are false positives from Markdown, example values, documentation links, and analytics terminology. The Facebook Pixel example loads third-party JavaScript and sends page-view telemetry when implemented. A separate consent-guidance gap could leave Custom HTML tracking active before consent; no evidence found of malicious instructions or credential theft.

remediation.issue: The Facebook Pixel example loads third-party JavaScript and records page views.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external script and telemetry destination, require site-owner approval, and restrict deployment to approved tracking purposes.

remediation.issue: Consent guidance implies automatic protection for all tags, while the Facebook Custom HTML example uses an All Pages trigger.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit marketing-consent checks for Facebook Custom HTML tags. Test initial denial, grant, and revocation in GTM Preview; Google consent settings alone are insufficient.

semantic_findings.title: Custom HTML consent enforcement is incomplete
semantic_findings.description: The guide says 'Tags respect consent state automatically' after consent configuration. Its Facebook Custom HTML example uses 'All Pages' without an explicit consent gate. Google consent settings alone do not stop this Custom HTML pixel, so copied configurations can track visitors before marketing consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example uses an unconditional All Pages trigger, and the consent section provides Google settings without showing Facebook-specific gating. This is a documented deployment risk, not evidence of actual visitor tracking by the skill.

content.user_title: Build and Audit Analytics Tracking Plans
content.value_statement: Inconsistent events and campaign labels make marketing and product results difficult to measure. This skill provides tracking plans, implementation examples, and validation guidance for GA4 and Google Tag Manager.
actual_capabilities: Draft tracking plans with event names, properties, triggers, custom dimensions, and conversion definitions.
Recommend event taxonomies for marketing sites, SaaS products, and e-commerce funnels.
Provide GA4 custom event examples and guidance for dimensions, audiences, and conversion counting.
Explain GTM tags, triggers, variables, data layer patterns, preview testing, and container versioning.
Define consistent UTM source, medium, campaign, content, and term conventions.
Guide debugging of missing events, incorrect properties, duplicate firing, and potential personal data exposure.
limitations: The package contains guidance and examples, not an installed analytics connector or an automated audit runner.
Live validation and account changes require authorized access, suitable tools, and your implementation environment.
Attribution modeling and experiment design are delegated to related skills, not covered in depth.
Privacy guidance does not establish legal compliance; Custom HTML pixels require explicit consent controls beyond Google consent settings.

use_cases.title: Standardize campaign measurement
use_cases.description: Define conversion events and UTM conventions for advertising, newsletters, and organic campaigns.

use_cases.title: Instrument product activation
use_cases.description: Create a SaaS tracking plan for signup, onboarding, feature usage, and subscription changes.

use_cases.title: Validate store tracking
use_cases.description: Map purchase properties and diagnose missing or duplicate events with GA4 DebugView and GTM Preview.

prompt_templates.title: Choose essential events
prompt_templates.prompt: We run a marketing website using GA4. Recommend five events for demo requests and signups. Include properties, triggers, and the decision each event supports.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish a focused event list.

prompt_templates.title: Define campaign labels
prompt_templates.prompt: Create UTM conventions for Google Ads, LinkedIn ads, and our newsletter. Define source, medium, campaign, and content values with examples and a documentation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose duplicate conversions
prompt_templates.prompt: Our GA4 signup event appears twice. We use GTM and application data layer events. Outline checks for duplicate tags, trigger conditions, and conversion counting.

prompt_templates.title: Design an implementation review
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GA4 and GTM tracking plan for an online store. Include purchase properties, dimensions, deduplication checks, explicit pixel consent gates, and deployment validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate implementation and privacy review.

output_examples.input: What should we track for SaaS signup and activation?
output: Signup completed: fire after successful account creation; record signup method and plan without email addresses.
Onboarding step completed: record step number and step name to identify onboarding drop-off.
Feature used: record feature name and category to compare activation behavior.
Validation: confirm each intended action produces one event with expected properties in GA4 DebugView.

output_examples.input: Our purchase event fires twice in GTM.
output: Inspect GTM Preview to identify every tag firing for a single purchase.
Check duplicate containers, overlapping triggers, and repeated application data layer pushes.
Verify transaction identifiers and review the configured conversion counting method.
Retest one purchase across browsers and mobile before publishing the container version.

output_examples.input: Create UTM conventions for our newsletter and search ads.
output: Newsletter: source newsletter, medium email, campaign product_launch, content footer_cta.
Search ads: source google, medium cpc, campaign product_launch, term matching the paid keyword.
Use lowercase values and document approved labels in a shared campaign spreadsheet.

best_practices: Start with business decisions, then document the smallest useful set of events and properties.
Validate event triggers, property values, and duplicate behavior in GTM Preview and GA4 DebugView before publication.
Exclude personal data and test explicit consent gating for each analytics or marketing tag, including Custom HTML pixels.
anti_patterns: Tracking every interaction without defining which decision it supports.
Using inconsistent event names or UTM labels across teams and channels.
Publishing third-party pixels on All Pages while assuming Google consent settings automatically block them.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically connect to my analytics accounts?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples; account access requires separately configured tools and authorization.

faq.question: Which analytics tools receive detailed coverage?
faq.answer: GA4 and Google Tag Manager have bundled implementation references. Other analytics tools are listed with external guide links.

faq.question: Can it help diagnose duplicate events?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides checks for duplicate containers, repeated triggers, variable paths, and event validation using preview and debugging tools.

faq.question: Does it guarantee privacy compliance?
faq.answer: No. Review legal requirements, minimize data collection, and explicitly gate third-party pixels with the appropriate consent controls.

faq.question: Does it cover attribution models or experiment design?
faq.answer: Not in depth. It directs attribution questions and experiment design to related skills while supporting tracking implementation.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide your tools, technology stack, existing tracking, key conversions, business decisions, and consent requirements. Relevant local product-marketing context can reduce repeated questions.
